data.current_summary: Read the progress of an async create/update operation
data.current_description:
Async mode (SPEC section 5.9.3): when a create or update call was made with async=1 (or a callbackUrl, which implies it), the 202 answer hands back an operationId; this endpoint tells the integrator when the deferred document downloads landed and whether the automations fired.

The document URLs are never part of the payload (they can carry signed tokens): each entry exposes the tag it targets, its state, and either the written documentId or the error. An operation of another organization answers 404 (never 403), and so does an operation past its retention (7 days after completion).

Recommended polling cadence: every 5 seconds, at most every 2 minutes; a callbackUrl saves the polling altogether. The signed callback pushes the very same payload.
data.summary_suggestion: Poll the status of an asynchronous operation
data.description_suggestion:
Retrieves the current status and progress of an asynchronous create or update operation. Returns an OperationStatus object containing the state of each deferred document (tag, completion state, document ID or error), and whether associated automations have fired.

Input: operationId (required) - the operation identifier returned in the 202 response from an async create/update request.

Output: OperationStatus object with document-level details including tag, state, documentId (on success), and error information (on failure).

Side effects: None. This is a read-only polling endpoint. Operations are retained for 7 days after completion; requests for expired or non-existent operations return 404. Cross-organization access returns 404 (not 403).

Recommended polling interval: 5-120 seconds. Alternatively, use a callbackUrl in the original request to receive push notifications instead of polling.

data.current_summary: Read the progress of an async create/update operation
data.current_description:
Async mode (SPEC section 5.9.3): when a create or update call was made with async=1 (or a callbackUrl, which implies it), the 202 answer hands back an operationId; this endpoint tells the integrator when the deferred document downloads landed and whether the automations fired.

The document URLs are never part of the payload (they can carry signed tokens): each entry exposes the tag it targets, its state, and either the written documentId or the error. An operation of another organization answers 404 (never 403), and so does an operation past its retention (7 days after completion).

Recommended polling cadence: every 5 seconds, at most every 2 minutes; a callbackUrl saves the polling altogether. The signed callback pushes the very same payload.
data.summary_suggestion: Poll the status of an asynchronous operation
data.description_suggestion:
Retrieves the current status and progress of an asynchronous create or update operation. Returns an OperationStatus object containing the state of each deferred document (tag, completion state, document ID or error), and whether associated automations have fired.

Input: operationId (required) - the operation identifier returned in the 202 response from an async create/update request.

Output: OperationStatus object with document-level details including tag, state, documentId (on success), and error information (on failure).

Side effects: None. This is a read-only polling endpoint. Operations are retained for 7 days after completion; requests for expired or non-existent operations return 404. Cross-organization access returns 404 (not 403).

Recommended polling interval: 5-120 seconds. Alternatively, use a callbackUrl in the original request to receive push notifications instead of polling.

data.current_description:
The id in the PATH is the only thing that makes this an update (no verb in the URL, no PATCH). MERGE semantics: a field present in the body overwrites the stored value, an ABSENT field is left UNCHANGED, an explicitly NULL field ERASES it — except categories, where null is refused with 400 (the storage layer cannot erase categories).

categories, when present, replaces the whole set and every id must belong to the organization; when absent, the existing categories are kept untouched. creatorUserId is NOT modifiable on update and is silently ignored (changing the creator changes who SEES the company in the UI — that is a data-takeover, not a company update).

A company of another organization answers 404 (never 403): no cross-organization enumeration signal. A company carried by a LOCKED process (read-only record) answers 423 company_locked.

X-Profile-Token is not used on this resource: the header is silently ignored.

Categories, when provided, replace the entire set. CreatorUserId is ignored and cannot be modified.
